entries.title: prove deflate and inflate's panic sites
entries.body:
std/compress/deflate.ts goes from 398 unproven panic sites to the five kept caller-misuse panics: a window outside its array, a level outside 0 to 9, and a negative limit. The bit-buffer and window arithmetic now carries bounds the prover accepts. The Huffman and length builders report a bad table instead of panicking. An encoder store that does not fit sets an overrun flag, which compress answers as DEFLATE_NO_ROOM, so output is never silently cut short. A corrupt or truncated stream still answers its DEFLATE_ERR_* code.

deflateBound, compressBound and fixedDeflateBound answer -1 only past the largest input whose bound fits in i32: 2,146,664,744, 2,146,664,726 and 1,908,874,339. Every bound gzip.ts relies on stays a real size. tests/link/std_compress_deflate_bounds pins each edge.

Measured: instructions (cachegrind, CI runner): std-compress-deflate 203,069,611 → 166,095,944 (-18.2%), std-compress-inflate 249,172,164 → 219,002,920 (-12.1%), std-compress-gzip 189,410,010 → 162,588,277 (-14.2%)
Tests: tests/link/std_compress_deflate_bounds
Verified: pr-adversary 2 rounds, CI green

Fixes #2153
entries.author: Redis Stasa

entries.title: file the router prover performance plan
entries.body:
Plans the fix for the std-router regression from the panic-free sweep
(155,580,314 to 162,304,316 instructions, +4.32%). The range prover learns
the facts the router's hand-written guards restate: bounds carried around
while loops, exit facts out of private callees, and ranged private fields.
The guards those facts prove are then deleted. Filed as #2220 with stages
#2221 to #2226; S5 (parallel arrays) waits on a decision.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: space code blocks inside steps and details
entries.body:
Scalar spaces only the direct children of .t-prose, so inside a step or a
collapsible a code block touched the paragraph after it. The theme now gives
those children the same 18px block spacing.

The site's favicons are listed largest first, since Scalar drops the sizes
attribute from head links, and the guide's compiler diagnostics are fenced
as log so Scalar's log grammar can colour them.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: grant ci-gate's statuses: write to the release run
entries.body:
The 0.45.0 release run failed at startup, before any job ran. ci.yml's
ci-gate job now asks for `statuses: write`, to report a `ci-gate` commit
status on a dispatched run, but release.yml's `ci` job, which calls
ci.yml, granted only `contents: read` and `attestations: read`. A called
workflow's job may not ask for more than its caller grants, so GitHub
refused the whole run. The `ci` job now grants `statuses: write` too.

A new check, `node tests/run.js workflow-permissions`, reads every job
that calls a local workflow and fails when the callee's top-level
permissions, or any of its jobs' own, ask for a scope the caller does not
grant. It names the caller, the callee job and the missing scope.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon
